title: SOC Workbench (Agentic SOC): alert unification, correlation and prioritization, and what can be automated

prose.label: Sources.
prose.text: Which third-party tools can feed it is not captured: [[aem.secops-platform:connector-catalog]].
{{no-client-surface}} Its reports are exported through the platform's Reporting API, [[aem.secops-platform:reporting-api]], whose contract is open: [[aem.secops-platform:reporting-api-contract]].

checks.do: Treat SOC Workbench and Agentic SOC as one product when matching help pages, console menus (SOC Workbench > My Reports) and questions.
For exporting incidents programmatically, use a saved report and the SecOps Reporting API; no client exposes SOC Workbench objects.

renamed.statement: The help article at the SOC Workbench address (/soc-workbench/what-zscaler-soc-workbench) is titled What Is Zscaler Agentic SOC?, and its sibling article is published under /agentic-soc; current help calls the product Agentic SOC.
renamed.conditions: Rests on the captured titles and URLs; no captured page states the rename in words.

what-it-is.statement: Agentic SOC is a unified platform that uses a multi-agentic AI approach to prioritize and triage threats, with risk-based prioritization that weighs a threat's business context.

quotes: Agentic SOC uses a multi-agentic AI approach to provide rich, context-driven data
Agentic SOC is a unified platform to prioritize and triage threats so that you can rapidly resolve business-critical incidents.
Agentic SOC provides risk-based prioritization that focuses not only on a threat but also its business context.

unify-alerts.statement: It tracks Zscaler alerts and alerts from third-party applications (for example Gmail and CrowdStrike) in a single console, with visibility across assets, identities and exposures.

quotes: Agentic SOC lets you track not only Zscaler alerts, but also alerts from third-party applications (e.g., Gmail, CrowdStrike) in a single console
Agentic SOC provides visibility across assets, identities, and exposures in a unified application.

data-fabric-and-zte.statement: It is powered by the Zscaler Data Fabric for Security, and its integration with the Zero Trust Exchange adds threat context and initiates inline controls to mitigate risk automatically.

quotes: Powered by the Zscaler Data Fabric for Security, Agentic SOC transforms isolated alerts from across your security stack into a prioritized, holistic view of threats.
Seamless integration with the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) platform provides additional threat context and initiates inline controls to automatically mitigate risk.

exposure-context.statement: As part of the Agentic SecOps Platform portfolio, it connects exposure insights with threat prioritization, so vulnerable assets and identities are factored into weighted results.

quotes: As part of the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform) portfolio, Agentic SOC also connects exposure insights with threat prioritization, ensuring that vulnerable assets and identities are factored into weighted results.

workflow.statement: It pulls first-party data from Zscaler products and integrates with third-party solutions, enriches each alert with identity, asset, location and threat-intelligence metadata at the fabric layer, groups alerts into incidents, and scores incidents by risk.

quotes: Agentic SOC pulls in first-party data from Zscaler products and integrates seamlessly with third-party solutions.
Each alert is enhanced with contextual metadata (like identity, asset, location, and threat intelligence) at the fabric layer.
Alerts are analyzed and intelligently grouped into incidents, representing the full attack story rather than isolated data points.
Risk-based scoring identifies high-priority incidents requiring immediate action

first-five.statement: Its AI-driven threat analysis turns raw alerts into contextualized threats and uses historical attack patterns to identify the first 5 things to address.

quotes: Agentic SOC's AI-driven threat analysis transforms raw alerts into contextualized, actionable threats.
leveraging historical attack patterns to identify the first 5 things you must address in your environment.

investigation.statement: Investigation shows all threat details on a single page, with log search from one place and the asset impact on the same page.

quotes: providing all threat details on a single page, as well as the ability to search logs from one unified location, understand the asset impact on the same page

response-agent.statement: The AI Response Agent takes triaged incidents and provides targeted remediation recommendations.

quotes: Agentic SOC's AI Response Agent takes triaged incidents and provides targeted remediation recommendations

no-client-surface.statement: No vendored client covers SOC Workbench or Agentic SOC: the Go and Python SDKs, the Terraform providers, the Ansible collections, the MCP server, the OneAPI Postman collection and the captured Automate contract have no such service.

quotes: used in your server-side code to interact with the Zscaler API platform across multiple products such as:

no-client-surface.conditions: Rests on an absence. The Python README's product list (introduced by the quoted line) names neither, and at the pins `git grep -i -E 'soc.workbench|agentic.soc'` finds nothing in the Go or Python SDKs, the ZIA, ZPA, ZCC or ZTC providers, the Ansible collections or the MCP server; the Postman collection has no match. The MCP server's Z-Insights tools report aggregate analytics and are a separate product.
